questions.stem: The combined oral contraceptive pill contains synthetic oestrogen and progesterone. How does the oestrogen component prevent pregnancy?

options.text: It kills sperm cells in the reproductive tract
It inhibits FSH release from the pituitary gland, preventing follicle development and ovulation
It thickens the uterus lining so the embryo cannot implant
It blocks the fallopian tubes physically

questions.explanation: The synthetic oestrogen in the pill maintains artificially high oestrogen levels, which inhibit the pituitary gland from releasing FSH. Without FSH, no follicle matures in the ovary and no egg is released (ovulation is prevented). This is hormonal contraception using negative feedback.

questions.stem: A couple decides to use condoms as their contraceptive method. Which statement correctly describes how condoms prevent pregnancy and an additional benefit they provide?

options.text: Condoms release hormones that prevent ovulation and also protect against STIs
Condoms are a barrier method that prevents sperm reaching the egg and also protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs)
Condoms dissolve sperm chemically and prevent implantation
Condoms are only effective when used with hormonal contraception

questions.explanation: Condoms are a barrier method — they physically prevent sperm from entering the female reproductive tract and reaching the egg. Unlike hormonal methods, condoms also provide protection against STIs (sexually transmitted infections) such as chlamydia and HIV.

questions.stem: An intrauterine device (IUD) made of copper is inserted into the uterus. How does a copper IUD prevent pregnancy?

options.text: It releases hormones that prevent ovulation
It physically blocks the cervix so sperm cannot enter
Copper ions are toxic to sperm and also prevent a fertilised egg from implanting in the uterus lining
It absorbs the egg before it can be fertilised

questions.explanation: A copper IUD works in two ways: the copper ions released are toxic to sperm (reducing their motility and viability), and the IUD creates an inflammatory response in the uterus that prevents implantation of a fertilised egg. It does not contain hormones.

questions.stem: A woman is prescribed the progesterone-only pill. Which effects does progesterone have that help prevent pregnancy?

options.text: It stimulates the release of FSH and LH to prevent ovulation
It thickens cervical mucus (making it difficult for sperm to pass through) and thins the uterus lining
It causes the fallopian tubes to close permanently
It directly destroys any eggs released by the ovary

questions.explanation: Progesterone thickens the cervical mucus, creating a barrier that sperm find difficult to penetrate. It also thins the uterus lining, making implantation less likely. In some cases, it may also suppress ovulation. These combined effects reduce the chance of pregnancy.

questions.stem: A couple is choosing between hormonal and non-hormonal contraception. The woman has a history of blood clots. Why might her doctor advise against the combined pill?

options.text: The combined pill is less effective than other methods
The synthetic oestrogen in the combined pill can increase the risk of blood clots in susceptible individuals
The combined pill causes permanent infertility
The combined pill only works for women under 30

questions.explanation: The oestrogen component of the combined pill carries a small increased risk of blood clots (thrombosis). For women with a history of blood clots or certain risk factors, this risk may be unacceptable. The doctor might recommend the progesterone-only pill, an IUD, or a barrier method instead.
